name: 'An evening with Hon. Bob Chiarelli, MPP and Hon. Charles Sousa, MPP' – $7,500-a-ticket Ontario Liberal fundraiser, Toronto (Dec 7, 2015)
summary: Ontario Finance Minister Charles Sousa and Energy Minister Bob Chiarelli attended an invitation-only Ontario Liberal fundraiser one month after the Hydro One IPO. Per the Integrity Commissioner's report, 24 people from financial institutions, unions, government-relations firms and the energy sector paid $7,500 each; nine of the 16 banks involved in the Hydro One offerings had representatives there; the honorary chair was John Sherrington of Scotiabank. The Globe and Mail reported the event was a two-hour cocktail reception and dinner, and that the Liberals' Elections Ontario filing listed only a $4,000 event that day. Commissioner J. David Wake found no contravention of s.6 of the Members' Integrity Act but called for a review of the Act.

name: Liberal $1,500 private fundraiser with PM Justin Trudeau at Benson Wong's home, Toronto (May 19, 2016)
summary: The Globe and Mail reported that Prime Minister Justin Trudeau was the top draw at a $1,500 Liberal Party fundraiser at the Toronto home of Benson Wong, chair of the Chinese Business Chamber of Canada, attended by 32 other people. Guests included Zhang Bin (a political adviser to the Chinese government) who, with Niu Gensheng, pledged $1 million to the Pierre Elliott Trudeau Foundation and the University of Montreal law faculty weeks later; the Globe found no evidence Zhang paid to attend. Also present per the Globe: Shenglin Xian (founder of Wealth One Bank, then awaiting regulatory approval), Bob Guo and Liu Meng. The Tyee reported attendees paid a reported $1,525. A later Globe report said invitees were asked for $4,500-$5,000, above the contribution limit.

name: Liberal $1,500 fundraiser with PM Justin Trudeau at Miaofei Pan's home, West Vancouver (Nov 7, 2016)
summary: The Globe and Mail reported that developer Miaofei Pan hosted a $1,500-a-ticket Liberal fundraiser at his West Vancouver home on Nov. 7, 2016, where more than 80 guests dined and were photographed with Prime Minister Justin Trudeau. Pan told the Globe he lobbied Trudeau on investment in seniors' care, investor-immigration rules and foreign real-estate investment. The event was not listed by the PMO or party. The Tyee and iPolitics reported Pan's account (to a Wenzhou newspaper) that Trudeau's invitation to a dinner for Premier Li Keqiang prompted the fundraiser; the Liberal Party called that 'categorically false'.

summary: The Calgary Herald reported Premier Danielle Smith spoke to a sold-out crowd of more than 900 at the $250-per-ticket UCP Leader's Dinner at a Calgary hotel on March 22, 2023, the first Leader's Dinner for a sitting Tory government in Alberta since 2015 (Jason Kenney had declined to continue the events). She reiterated support for a new Flames arena and an airport CTrain link. A 2024 UCP advisory (per the Herald) put the 2023 attendance at 950.

name: UCP second annual Calgary Leader's Dinner with Premier Danielle Smith, $500 a plate (Apr 3, 2024)
summary: The United Conservative Party held its second annual Calgary Leader's Dinner with Premier Danielle Smith at the BMO Centre on April 3, 2024. The Calgary Herald reported the sold-out $500-a-plate dinner drew more than 1,300 and, per organizers, raised $663,000, twice the previous year; the UCP said the prior year's event drew 950. CityNews reported over 1,350 attendees and estimated earnings topping $675,000. Smith gave the keynote. The Edmonton Leader's Dinner was set for April 16 at $350 a plate.

name: UCP second annual Edmonton Leader's Dinner with Premier Danielle Smith, $350 a plate (Apr 16, 2024)
summary: The Edmonton Journal reported Premier Danielle Smith hosted the UCP's second annual Edmonton Leader's Dinner on Tuesday Apr 16, 2024 at the Edmonton Convention Centre, which the party said drew around 1,300 people. MLA Shane Getson told the crowd the event had raised $455,000, with the party hoping to add $100,000 via individual donations during the evening. Party president Rob Smith cited the $350-per-plate turnout. Before the event, the Calgary Herald reported it had sold 1,100 tickets at $350 a plate.
